message.content: In domestic cats and many wild felids—including lions—the **presence of a mane** (the long, shaggy fur that develops around the head, neck, and shoulders of adult males) is controlled by a dominant allele. Male lions that carry the dominant allele will develop a mane, while females (who are hemizygous for the X‑linked mane gene) typically do not. This dominant trait is one of the most striking phenotypic differences between male and female lions.
